limitations: Synthetic inode collisions do not prove an actual NTFS same-projection replacement; other directory metadata and native ACL checks remain real
The signed anchor only proves a signature relative to an explicitly supplied key; caller self-signing cannot establish root or tenant authority
Existing deployment loader/config/profile and operator registry roots remain caller/configuration-relative and are not reused as independently trusted tenant authority
Independent host root provisioning, durable routing pins, root/revision high-water and revocation, forced routing, and cross-host tenant uniqueness are not implemented
Checkpoint, restriction history, predecessor and storage graph fields are signed declarations; no runtime History replay or history-transfer proof is performed by these pure contracts
No authenticated RRSI producer, candidate alias preparation/finalization, Registry business writer or release source gate was enabled
Local HMAC/manifest fixtures, native permission checks and process recovery do not prove production key custody, external WORM or physical power-loss durability
No Linux/macOS release matrix, actual model/cost experiment or production promotion was run
